# Appsolutely Free — Complete Machine-Readable Software Directory

> Full plain-text catalog of 74 commercial software products and 267 verified free and open-source alternatives.
> Canonical URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/
> Published by: Yishay Stewart-Mitchell (Jamaica, Queens, NY)
> Updated: 2026-10-12

---

## 1. Figma
- Vendor: Figma, Inc.
- Category: Design & Illustration
- Typical Commercial Price: Free tier available; paid seats billed monthly
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/figma/
- Verified Free Alternatives (5 tools):
  * **Penpot** [https://penpot.app]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: MPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/penpot/penpot)
    - Summary: Browser-based design and prototyping tool for teams, built on open standards and available to self-host.
    - Advantages: Can be self-hosted, so files stay on your own server; Layout concepts mirror CSS flexbox and grid, which helps designer-developer handoff; Real-time collaboration and commenting
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Smaller plugin and template ecosystem than Figma; Self-hosting needs Docker and ongoing server upkeep
  * **Lunacy** [https://icons8.com/lunacy]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: Free
    - Summary: A free design tool for UI and graphics that opens Sketch files and includes built-in assets.
    - Advantages: Opens Sketch (.sketch) and Figma-style layouts; Offline use with built-in icons and stock; Free to use for design work
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Collaboration is lighter than Figma; Plugin ecosystem is small
  * **Vectr** [https://vectr.com/]
    - Platforms: web, windows, macos, linux
    - License: Free
    - Summary: A free, simple vector graphics editor that works in the browser or as a desktop app.
    - Advantages: Easy to learn for logos and icons; Real-time collaboration and sharing; Free web and desktop versions
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Far fewer features than Illustrator; Development has slowed in recent years
  * **AFFiNE** [https://affine.pro/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/toeverything/AFFiNE)
    - Summary: A next-gen privacy-first open-source workspace combining Notion-style docs, Miro-style whiteboards, and databases.
    - Advantages: Seamless switch between document view and infinite canvas whiteboard; Local-first with peer sync; No vendor lock-in
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Younger ecosystem than Notion; Self-hosting takes configuration
  * **Quant-UX** [https://www.quant-ux.com/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/KlausSchaefers/quant-ux)
    - Summary: An open-source visual prototyping and usability testing platform that records user test sessions with heatmaps and analytics.
    - Advantages: Create interactive screen prototypes and test them with real users; Visual heatmaps and recorded click sessions analyze user flow friction; 100% open-source and privacy-friendly
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Smaller component library than Figma Community; Learning curve for usability analytics configurations

---

## 2. Microsoft Office
- Vendor: Microsoft Corporation
- Category: Office & Documents
- Typical Commercial Price: Subscription or one-time purchase, depending on the edition
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/microsoft-office/
- Verified Free Alternatives (7 tools):
  * **Apache OpenOffice** [https://www.openoffice.org]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: Apache-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/apache/openoffice)
    - Summary: Long-running free office suite with a word processor, spreadsheet, presentations, drawing, and database tools.
    - Advantages: Free suite covering documents, spreadsheets, presentations, drawing, and databases; Opens common Microsoft Office file formats
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Releases are infrequent; the latest stable version, 4.1.16, is from November 2025; Some Microsoft Office formatting may not carry over; LibreOffice is more actively maintained
  * **OnlyOffice** [https://www.onlyoffice.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: AGPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/ONLYOFFICE/DocumentServer)
    - Summary: A free and open-source office suite that is highly compatible with Microsoft Office formats. Available on desktop, web, and mobile.
  * **LibreOffice** [https://www.libreoffice.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: MPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/LibreOffice/core)
    - Summary: The full-featured free office suite with word processing, spreadsheets, slides, and drawing.
    - Advantages: Writer, Calc, Impress, Draw, and Base; Opens and saves Microsoft Office formats; No account or subscription
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Interface looks traditional; Complex Office documents may shift slightly
  * **Google Docs, Sheets & Slides** [https://workspace.google.com/products/docs/]
    - Platforms: web, ios, android
    - License: Free with a Google account
    - Summary: Free online word processing, spreadsheets, and presentations with real-time collaboration.
    - Advantages: Real-time collaboration out of the box; Autosave and version history; Opens and exports Office formats
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Needs an internet connection for best results; Fewer advanced Excel and Word features
  * **Microsoft 365 for the web** [https://www.microsoft365.com/free-office-online-for-the-web]
    - Platforms: web, ios, android
    - License: Free with a Microsoft account
    - Summary: Free browser versions of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint with 5 GB of OneDrive storage.
    - Advantages: Real Office file fidelity; Free with a Microsoft account; Co-authoring and OneDrive sync
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Missing many desktop features; Includes some ads and upsells
  * **WPS Office** [https://www.wps.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: Free with ads, paid Premium
    - Summary: A lightweight office suite with Writer, Spreadsheet, and Presentation that looks like Microsoft Office.
    - Advantages: Familiar Office-style ribbon; Handles docx, xlsx, pptx, and PDF; Runs on desktop and mobile
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Free version shows ads; Some features require a subscription
  * **Apple Pages, Numbers & Keynote** [https://www.apple.com/iwork/]
    - Platforms: macos, ios, web
    - License: Free on Apple devices
    - Summary: Apple’s free suite for documents, spreadsheets, and beautiful presentations.
    - Advantages: Polished templates and design; Free on every Apple device; iCloud collaboration
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Best on Apple devices; Some Office formatting may shift when exporting

---

## 3. Photoshop
- Vendor: Adobe Inc.
- Category: Design & Illustration
- Typical Commercial Price: Monthly subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/photoshop/
- Verified Free Alternatives (11 tools):
  * **PhotoCraft** [https://getartcraft.com/apps/photocraft]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, web
    - License: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/storytold/photocraft)
    - Summary: Native, offline image editor with layers, masks, adjustment layers, and layered PSD support, laid out like Photoshop.
    - Advantages: Menus and shortcuts follow Photoshop's layout; Opens and saves layered PSD and PSB files; Runs offline with no account
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Early alpha; the project says it is not yet a replacement for daily professional work; No generative AI features; About twenty tools and plug-in compatibility are still missing
  * **GIMP** [https://www.gimp.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0
    - Summary: The classic free image editor with layers, masks, filters, and scripting for serious photo work.
    - Advantages: Layers, masks, curves, and a huge filter set; Reads and writes PSD files; Scriptable with Python and Script-Fu
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Interface feels different from Photoshop; Non-destructive editing is more limited
  * **Krita** [https://krita.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, android
    - License: GPL-3.0
    - Summary: A professional painting and illustration app built by artists, with fantastic brush engines.
    - Advantages: Industry-grade brush engine; Animation tools and vector layers; Great tablet and pen support
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Less suited to photo retouching than GIMP; Heavier on large canvases
  * **Photopea** [https://www.photopea.com/]
    - Platforms: web
    - License: Free with ads
    - Summary: A free Photoshop-style editor that runs entirely in your browser and opens PSD, AI, XD, Sketch, and RAW files.
    - Advantages: Looks and feels like Photoshop, so there is almost no learning curve; Opens and saves PSD files with layers intact; Nothing to install; works on any computer with a browser
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Free version shows ads (a paid plan removes them); Heavy files depend on your browser and RAM
  * **Pixlr** [https://pixlr.com/]
    - Platforms: web, ios, android
    - License: Free tier, paid upgrade
    - Summary: Browser-based photo editor with layers, one-click effects, and AI tools, from quick fixes to full editing.
    - Advantages: Pixlr E offers a fuller editor, Pixlr X is simple and quick; Works in any browser and on mobile; Templates and AI cutout tools
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Some AI features are limited on the free tier; Free version includes ads
  * **Paint.NET** [https://www.getpaint.net/]
    - Platforms: windows
    - License: Freeware
    - Summary: A fast, friendly image editor for Windows with layers, effects, and a big plugin community.
    - Advantages: Very quick to learn and light on resources; Layers, blend modes, and plugins; No subscription for the full program
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Windows only; Less powerful than Photoshop for advanced retouching
  * **Affinity by Canva** [https://www.affinity.studio/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos
    - License: Free (account required)
    - Summary: A professional photo, vector, and layout suite that Canva made free to use.
    - Advantages: Pro-level raster, vector, and layout tools in one app; Imports PSD and AI files; No subscription
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Some AI features need a paid Canva plan; Requires a free Canva account
  * **Canva** [https://www.canva.com/]
    - Platforms: web, ios, android, windows, macos
    - License: Free tier, paid Pro
    - Summary: Drag-and-drop design for social posts, slides, logos, and posters, with a huge template library.
    - Advantages: Thousands of free templates; Easy for non-designers; great for social media; Real-time collaboration
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Not a true replacement for pixel-level editing; Best assets and Magic tools need Pro
  * **Pinta** [https://www.pinta-project.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/PintaProject/Pinta)
    - Summary: A simple, cross-platform image editor inspired by Paint.NET with layers and common adjustments.
    - Advantages: Clean, beginner-friendly interface; Layers, selections, and effects; Open source on Windows, Mac, and Linux
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Limited advanced features; Smaller plugin ecosystem
  * **Photoshop Express** [https://www.adobe.com/products/photoshop-express.html]
    - Platforms: ios, android, web, windows
    - License: Free tier, paid upgrade
    - Summary: Adobe’s free, simple photo editor for quick edits, filters, and collages on your phone or PC.
    - Advantages: Fast fixes with filters, crop, and healing; Familiar Adobe quality; Free on phone and PC
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Premium features are paid; Far fewer tools than full Photoshop
  * **Snapseed** [https://apps.apple.com/app/snapseed/id439438619]
    - Platforms: ios, android
    - License: Free
    - Summary: Google’s free mobile photo editor with selective adjustments, healing, and RAW support.
    - Advantages: Selective editing with control points; Free with no subscription; Open and edit RAW (DNG) files
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Mobile only; No library or cloud sync

---

## 4. Premiere Pro
- Vendor: Adobe Inc.
- Category: Video & Animation
- Typical Commercial Price: Monthly subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/premiere-pro/
- Verified Free Alternatives (7 tools):
  * **FilmCraft** [https://getartcraft.com/apps/filmcraft]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, web
    - License: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft)
    - Summary: Native video editor with Premiere-style panels, trim tools, color grading, and its own built-in codecs.
    - Advantages: Premiere-style workspaces, tools, and keyboard shortcuts; Exchanges timelines as Final Cut XML, OpenTimelineIO, EDL, and AAF; Color grading panel with live scopes
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: The project estimates it is about 50 to 60 percent ready for real work; No plugin hosting such as VST3, Audio Units, or OpenFX; H.264 is the only delivery-codec export; Hardware decoding works on macOS only
  * **Kdenlive** [https://kdenlive.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/KDE/kdenlive)
    - Summary: A multi-track video editor with proxies, keyframes, and a flexible timeline.
    - Advantages: Multi-track timeline and proxy editing; Wide format support through FFmpeg; Keyframeable effects
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Can be unstable on very complex projects; Hardware acceleration varies by system
  * **Shotcut** [https://shotcut.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/mltframework/shotcut)
    - Summary: A fast cross-platform video editor with a clean interface and broad format support.
    - Advantages: Native timeline editing, no import needed; Good filters and color tools; Portable version available
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Less polished than commercial editors; Fewer templates and effects
  * **DaVinci Resolve** [https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: Free version, paid Studio
    - Summary: A professional editor with industry-leading color grading, Fusion effects, and Fairlight audio, all in one free app.
    - Advantages: Hollywood-grade color, VFX, and audio tools; Free version has no watermark; Great performance on Mac, Windows, and Linux
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Needs a fairly powerful computer; A few features (like some codecs and AI) require Studio
  * **CapCut** [https://www.capcut.com/]
    - Platforms: web, windows, macos, ios, android
    - License: Free tier, paid Pro
    - Summary: An easy video editor with templates, auto captions, and effects, popular for social video.
    - Advantages: Quick editing with auto captions and templates; Works on phone, PC, and web; Large effects and music library
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Some effects and exports need Pro; Cloud features tie you to the platform
  * **Clipchamp** [https://clipchamp.com/]
    - Platforms: web, windows
    - License: Free tier, paid upgrade
    - Summary: A browser-based video editor from Microsoft with screen recording, templates, and 1080p export.
    - Advantages: Free 1080p exports without a watermark; Built-in screen and webcam recorder; Included with Windows 11
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Fewer pro features than desktop editors; 4K export requires a paid plan
  * **iMovie** [https://www.apple.com/imovie/]
    - Platforms: macos, ios
    - License: Free on Apple devices
    - Summary: Apple’s free video editor for Mac, iPhone, and iPad with trailers, titles, and 4K support.
    - Advantages: Free and preinstalled on Apple devices; Simple timeline with great templates; Projects move between iPhone and Mac
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Apple platforms only; Limited advanced editing and effects

---

## 5. Adobe Illustrator
- Vendor: Adobe
- Category: Design & Illustration
- Typical Commercial Price: Monthly or annual subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/illustrator/
- Verified Free Alternatives (7 tools):
  * **Krita** [https://krita.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, android
    - License: GPL-3.0
    - Summary: A professional painting and illustration app built by artists, with fantastic brush engines.
    - Advantages: Industry-grade brush engine; Animation tools and vector layers; Great tablet and pen support
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Less suited to photo retouching than GIMP; Heavier on large canvases
  * **Inkscape** [https://inkscape.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0
    - Summary: A powerful vector graphics editor for logos, icons, and illustrations using the open SVG format.
    - Advantages: Native SVG workflow; Bezier, node, and path tools; Extensible with plugins
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Can slow down on very complex files; CMYK workflow is limited
  * **Photopea** [https://www.photopea.com/]
    - Platforms: web
    - License: Free with ads
    - Summary: A free Photoshop-style editor that runs entirely in your browser and opens PSD, AI, XD, Sketch, and RAW files.
    - Advantages: Looks and feels like Photoshop, so there is almost no learning curve; Opens and saves PSD files with layers intact; Nothing to install; works on any computer with a browser
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Free version shows ads (a paid plan removes them); Heavy files depend on your browser and RAM
  * **Affinity by Canva** [https://www.affinity.studio/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos
    - License: Free (account required)
    - Summary: A professional photo, vector, and layout suite that Canva made free to use.
    - Advantages: Pro-level raster, vector, and layout tools in one app; Imports PSD and AI files; No subscription
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Some AI features need a paid Canva plan; Requires a free Canva account
  * **Canva** [https://www.canva.com/]
    - Platforms: web, ios, android, windows, macos
    - License: Free tier, paid Pro
    - Summary: Drag-and-drop design for social posts, slides, logos, and posters, with a huge template library.
    - Advantages: Thousands of free templates; Easy for non-designers; great for social media; Real-time collaboration
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Not a true replacement for pixel-level editing; Best assets and Magic tools need Pro
  * **Lunacy** [https://icons8.com/lunacy]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: Free
    - Summary: A free design tool for UI and graphics that opens Sketch files and includes built-in assets.
    - Advantages: Opens Sketch (.sketch) and Figma-style layouts; Offline use with built-in icons and stock; Free to use for design work
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Collaboration is lighter than Figma; Plugin ecosystem is small
  * **Vectr** [https://vectr.com/]
    - Platforms: web, windows, macos, linux
    - License: Free
    - Summary: A free, simple vector graphics editor that works in the browser or as a desktop app.
    - Advantages: Easy to learn for logos and icons; Real-time collaboration and sharing; Free web and desktop versions
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Far fewer features than Illustrator; Development has slowed in recent years

## 6. Adobe Lightroom
- Vendor: Adobe
- Category: Photo Editing
- Typical Commercial Price: Monthly or annual subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/lightroom/
- Verified Free Alternatives (5 tools):
  * **darktable** [https://www.darktable.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/darktable-org/darktable)
    - Summary: A RAW photo workflow app with non-destructive editing, tethering, and lens corrections.
    - Advantages: Non-destructive RAW development; Powerful masking and color tools; Tethered shooting support
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Steeper learning curve than Lightroom; No built-in cloud sync
  * **RawTherapee** [https://www.rawtherapee.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/RawTherapee/RawTherapee)
    - Summary: A cross-platform RAW converter focused on image quality and fine control of every parameter.
    - Advantages: Excellent demosaicing and detail; Batch processing and profiles; Very precise color control
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Interface is dense; Weaker photo library features
  * **Pixlr** [https://pixlr.com/]
    - Platforms: web, ios, android
    - License: Free tier, paid upgrade
    - Summary: Browser-based photo editor with layers, one-click effects, and AI tools, from quick fixes to full editing.
    - Advantages: Pixlr E offers a fuller editor, Pixlr X is simple and quick; Works in any browser and on mobile; Templates and AI cutout tools
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Some AI features are limited on the free tier; Free version includes ads
  * **Photoshop Express** [https://www.adobe.com/products/photoshop-express.html]
    - Platforms: ios, android, web, windows
    - License: Free tier, paid upgrade
    - Summary: Adobe’s free, simple photo editor for quick edits, filters, and collages on your phone or PC.
    - Advantages: Fast fixes with filters, crop, and healing; Familiar Adobe quality; Free on phone and PC
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Premium features are paid; Far fewer tools than full Photoshop
  * **Snapseed** [https://apps.apple.com/app/snapseed/id439438619]
    - Platforms: ios, android
    - License: Free
    - Summary: Google’s free mobile photo editor with selective adjustments, healing, and RAW support.
    - Advantages: Selective editing with control points; Free with no subscription; Open and edit RAW (DNG) files
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Mobile only; No library or cloud sync

## 7. After Effects
- Vendor: Adobe
- Category: Video & Animation
- Typical Commercial Price: Monthly or annual subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/after-effects/
- Verified Free Alternatives (4 tools):
  * **Blender** [https://www.blender.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/blender/blender)
    - Summary: A complete 3D suite for modeling, sculpting, animation, rendering, simulation, and video editing.
    - Advantages: Industry-proven modeling and rendering; Huge community and add-on market; Cycles and EEVEE render engines
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Big learning curve at the start; Some studio pipelines still expect Maya
  * **Natron** [https://natrongithub.github.io/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/NatronGitHub/Natron)
    - Summary: A node-based compositing app for visual effects and motion graphics.
    - Advantages: Node-based compositing workflow; Supports OpenFX plugins; Good for VFX pipelines
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Development is slower than commercial tools; Node workflow differs from layers
  * **DaVinci Resolve** [https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: Free version, paid Studio
    - Summary: A professional editor with industry-leading color grading, Fusion effects, and Fairlight audio, all in one free app.
    - Advantages: Hollywood-grade color, VFX, and audio tools; Free version has no watermark; Great performance on Mac, Windows, and Linux
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Needs a fairly powerful computer; A few features (like some codecs and AI) require Studio
  * **Cavalry** [https://cavalry.scenegroup.co/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos
    - License: Free starter tier, paid Pro
    - Summary: A next-generation 2D motion graphics and animation software built from the ground up for procedural motion design and UI animators.
    - Advantages: Procedural animation tools make complex particle and geometric animations effortless; Blazingly fast GPU-accelerated real-time viewport playback; Generous free tier with no time limit and full timeline export
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Free tier restricts renders to 1080p and disables certain advanced dynamics; Closed-source software

---

## 8. Final Cut Pro
- Vendor: Apple
- Category: Video & Animation
- Typical Commercial Price: One-time purchase, Mac only
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/final-cut-pro/
- Verified Free Alternatives (5 tools):
  * **Kdenlive** [https://kdenlive.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/KDE/kdenlive)
    - Summary: A multi-track video editor with proxies, keyframes, and a flexible timeline.
    - Advantages: Multi-track timeline and proxy editing; Wide format support through FFmpeg; Keyframeable effects
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Can be unstable on very complex projects; Hardware acceleration varies by system
  * **Shotcut** [https://shotcut.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/mltframework/shotcut)
    - Summary: A fast cross-platform video editor with a clean interface and broad format support.
    - Advantages: Native timeline editing, no import needed; Good filters and color tools; Portable version available
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Less polished than commercial editors; Fewer templates and effects
  * **OpenShot** [https://www.openshot.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/OpenShot/openshot-qt)
    - Summary: A beginner-friendly video editor with drag-and-drop clips, titles, and transitions.
    - Advantages: Very approachable for beginners; Animated titles and transitions; Cross-platform
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Struggles with heavy 4K projects; Fewer pro features
  * **DaVinci Resolve** [https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve]

    - License: Free version, paid Studio
    - Summary: A professional editor with industry-leading color grading, Fusion effects, and Fairlight audio, all in one free app.

  * **iMovie** [https://www.apple.com/imovie/]

    - License: Free on Apple devices
    - Summary: Apple’s free video editor for Mac, iPhone, and iPad with trailers, titles, and 4K support.
    - Advantages: Free and preinstalled on Apple devices; Simple timeline with great templates; Projects move between iPhone and Mac
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Apple platforms only; Limited advanced editing and effects

## 9. Camtasia
- Vendor: TechSmith
- Category: Video & Animation
- Typical Commercial Price: Paid license
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/camtasia/
- Verified Free Alternatives (6 tools):
  * **OpenShot** [https://www.openshot.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/OpenShot/openshot-qt)
    - Summary: A beginner-friendly video editor with drag-and-drop clips, titles, and transitions.
    - Advantages: Very approachable for beginners; Animated titles and transitions; Cross-platform
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Struggles with heavy 4K projects; Fewer pro features
  * **OBS Studio** [https://obsproject.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio)
    - Summary: The standard free tool for screen recording and live streaming, with scenes and plugins.
    - Advantages: Record and stream with scenes and sources; Huge plugin ecosystem; Low overhead and hardware encoding
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Recording only; editing needs another app; Setup takes some learning
  * **Clipchamp** [https://clipchamp.com/]
    - Platforms: web, windows
    - License: Free tier, paid upgrade
    - Summary: A browser-based video editor from Microsoft with screen recording, templates, and 1080p export.
    - Advantages: Free 1080p exports without a watermark; Built-in screen and webcam recorder; Included with Windows 11
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Fewer pro features than desktop editors; 4K export requires a paid plan
  * **Loom** [https://www.loom.com/]
    - Platforms: web, windows, macos, ios, android
    - License: Free tier, paid Business
    - Summary: Record your screen and camera and share a link instantly, ideal for walkthroughs and feedback.
    - Advantages: One-click record and share; Automatic transcripts on paid plans; Works in the browser and as an app
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Free plan limits video length and count; Editing tools are basic
  * **HandBrake** [https://handbrake.fr/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/HandBrake/HandBrake)
    - Summary: The open-source video transcoder for converting video from nearly any format to a selection of modern codecs.
    - Advantages: Massive preset library for devices, web, and streaming; Hardware encoding (NVENC, Intel QSV, Apple Silicon); Batch queue encoding
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Encoding only; does not edit or trim timelines; Cannot decrypt commercial copy-protected Blu-rays natively
  * **LosslessCut** [https://github.com/mifi/lossless-cut]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/mifi/lossless-cut)
    - Summary: The Swiss Army knife of lossless video, audio, and subtitle trimming that cuts files instantly at keyframes without re-encoding.
    - Advantages: Blazingly fast cuts in seconds with ZERO loss in video/audio quality; Extract audio tracks, subtitles, or create thumbnail chapters instantly; Supports virtually all video formats powered by FFmpeg
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Cuts only on video keyframes for pure lossless export; Not an effects editor or compositor

---

- Vendor: Adobe
- Category: Audio & Music

- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/adobe-audition/

    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/audacity/audacity)
    - Summary: The most popular free audio editor for recording, cleaning, and editing sound.

    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Editing is partly destructive; Interface looks dated
  * **Ardour** [https://ardour.org/]

    - Summary: A fast, easy audio editor with real-time effects and a clean waveform interface.
    - Advantages: Real-time effect previews; Handles large files quickly; Spectrogram and analysis tools

## 13. Sibelius
- Vendor: Avid
- Category: Audio & Music
- Typical Commercial Price: Subscription tiers
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/sibelius/
- Verified Free Alternatives (4 tools):
  * **MuseScore** [https://musescore.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/musescore/MuseScore)
    - Summary: A full-featured music notation app for composing, arranging, and printing scores.
    - Advantages: Professional engraving quality; MusicXML and MIDI import and export; Large online score community
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Fewer advanced layout tools than Sibelius; Plugin ecosystem is smaller
  * **LilyPond** [https://lilypond.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0
    - Summary: A music engraving system dedicated to producing the highest publication-quality sheet music from automated code input.
    - Advantages: Engraving quality matches the finest traditional European music publishers; Text-based music files can be version-controlled in Git; Automated spacing, beams, and collision avoidance
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Steep learning curve (text programming language, no visual piano roll); Requires a front-end like Frescobaldi for visual previews
  * **Flat.io** [https://flat.io/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: Free tier, paid Power
    - Summary: A collaborative online music score and guitar tablature editor that runs in your web browser with real-time multi-user editing.
    - Advantages: Real-time Google Docs-style collaboration on sheet music; Works in any browser on laptops, iPads, and Chromebooks; High-quality instrument playback audio
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Free plan limits you to 15 concurrent scores; Requires internet connection for cloud saving
  * **Noteflight** [https://www.noteflight.com/]
    - Platforms: web
    - License: Free tier, paid Crescendo
    - Summary: An established web-based music notation community and editor for writing, listening to, and sharing music online.
    - Advantages: Nothing to install; compose sheet music directly in your web browser; Active community to share and discover original scores; Print and export MIDI/XML files
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Free accounts are limited to 10 saved scores; Web interface can feel sluggish with huge orchestral scores

## 15. Autodesk Maya
- Vendor: Autodesk
- Category: 3D & CAD
- Typical Commercial Price: Costly annual subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/maya/
- Verified Free Alternatives (5 tools):
  * **Blender** [https://www.blender.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/blender/blender)
    - Summary: A complete 3D suite for modeling, sculpting, animation, rendering, simulation, and video editing.
    - Advantages: Industry-proven modeling and rendering; Huge community and add-on market; Cycles and EEVEE render engines
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Big learning curve at the start; Some studio pipelines still expect Maya
  * **Wings 3D** [http://www.wings3d.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: BSD-style
    - Summary: A dedicated polygon subdivision modeler with an intuitive contextual right-click interface and powerful mesh tools.
    - Advantages: Extremely fast and intuitive subdivision mesh modeling; Lightweight and boots up in a split second; Context-sensitive menus speed up polygon modeling workflows
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Modeling only: does not support animation or rigging; Traditional interface conventions
  * **MagicaVoxel** [https://ephtracy.github.io/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos
    - License: Freeware
    - Summary: A free, lightweight 8-bit voxel art editor and GPU-accelerated interactive path-tracing renderer that makes 3D creation accessible.
    - Advantages: Stunning built-in interactive path tracer with realistic shadows, glass, and emission; Extremely fun, accessible voxel block sculpting; Exports directly to OBJ, VOX, and MagicaVoxel formats
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Voxel aesthetic only; not suitable for traditional curved CAD/NURBS surfaces; No bone rigging system
  * **Dust3D** [https://dust3d.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/huxingyi/dust3d)
    - Summary: A quick 3D modeling software for indie game developers to auto-generate watertight base meshes, UV unwrap, and rig characters in minutes.
    - Advantages: Auto-generates clean 3D character meshes from 2D reference lines; Built-in automatic UV unwrapping and rigging; Exports directly to glTF and FBX for game engines
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Specialized for quick character base meshes, not detailed micro-sculpting; Interface takes an hour to get used to
  * **ArmorPaint** [https://armorpaint.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: zlib/libpng (free from source) (Repo: https://github.com/armory3d/armorpaint)
    - Summary: A stand-alone, GPU-accelerated 3D PBR texture painting software designed as an open-source alternative to Substance 3D Painter.
    - Advantages: Physically-based texture painting with real-time viewport feedback; Node-based procedural material graph editor; Runs smoothly on standard GPUs with ray tracing support
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Pre-compiled binaries require purchase/donation, though source code is completely free on GitHub; Smaller brush library than Substance Painter

## 17. MATLAB
- Vendor: MathWorks
- Category: Developer Tools
- Typical Commercial Price: Paid license plus toolboxes
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/matlab/
- Verified Free Alternatives (3 tools):
  * **GNU Octave** [https://octave.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0
    - Summary: A numerical computing language that is largely compatible with MATLAB scripts.
    - Advantages: Runs most MATLAB code with few changes; Strong math and plotting; Large package library
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Slower than MATLAB for some workloads; No Simulink equivalent
  * **Julia** [https://julialang.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia)
    - Summary: A fast, modern language for scientific computing with MATLAB-like syntax.
    - Advantages: Very fast numerical performance; MATLAB-like syntax for arrays; Rich package ecosystem
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Smaller ecosystem than Python; First-run compile latency
  * **Scilab** [https://www.scilab.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0 / CeCILL
    - Summary: Free software for numerical computation with Xcos, a Simulink-like block diagram tool.
    - Advantages: Xcos simulation like Simulink; MATLAB-style scripting; Free for any use
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Smaller toolbox ecosystem; Not fully MATLAB compatible

    - Summary: Run other operating systems in virtual machines on your desktop for free.
    - Advantages: Run Windows, Linux, and more; Snapshots and shared folders; Free and widely supported
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Apple Silicon support is limited; Slower graphics than Parallels
  * **UTM** [https://mac.getutm.app/]
    - Platforms: macos, ios
    - License: Apache-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/utmapp/UTM)
    - Summary: Run Windows, Linux, and more in virtual machines on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.
    - Advantages: Native on Apple Silicon; Runs many operating systems; Free outside the Mac App Store
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Slower graphics than Parallels; More manual setup
  * **VMware Workstation & Fusion** [https://www.vmware.com/products/desktop-hypervisor/workstation-and-fusion]
    - Platforms: windows, linux, macos
    - License: Free for personal use
    - Summary: A mature virtualization app that is free for personal use on Windows, Linux, and Mac.
    - Advantages: Excellent VM performance and compatibility; Snapshots and shared folders; Free for personal use
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Commercial use requires a license; Heavy install

    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Proprietary network relays; Smaller community than RustDesk

## 24. Snagit
- Vendor: TechSmith
- Category: System Utilities
- Typical Commercial Price: Paid license
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/snagit/
- Verified Free Alternatives (7 tools):
  * **ShareX** [https://getsharex.com/]
    - Platforms: windows
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/ShareX/ShareX)
    - Summary: A powerful screenshot and screen recording tool with annotations and instant uploads.
    - Advantages: Screenshots, GIFs, and screen recording; Automated workflows; Many upload destinations
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Windows only; Settings are overwhelming at first
  * **Flameshot** [https://flameshot.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/flameshot-org/flameshot)
    - Summary: A simple, customizable screenshot tool with built-in annotation and sharing.
    - Advantages: Quick annotations right on capture; Keyboard-friendly; Cross-platform
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: No video capture; Fewer editing tools than Snagit
  * **Greenshot** [https://getgreenshot.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/greenshot/greenshot)
    - Summary: A lightweight screenshot tool with quick annotations and one-click export.
    - Advantages: Quick region capture and annotations; Exports to files, clipboard, and apps; Light on resources
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: No video recording; Fewer editing tools than Snagit
  * **Lightshot** [https://app.prntscr.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos
    - License: Free
    - Summary: A fast, free screenshot tool with simple editing and instant sharing.
    - Advantages: One-key capture and upload; Basic annotations; Reverse image search
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Limited editing; Uploads go to a public server by default
  * **Screenity** [https://screenity.io/]
    - Platforms: web
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/alyssaxuu/screenity)
    - Summary: A feature-packed open-source screen recorder and annotation tool for Chrome with webcam overlay, zoom, drawing, and trimming.
    - Advantages: Unlimited recordings with zero watermarks or time limits; Annotate your screen live with pens, arrows, text, and click highlights; Save directly to Google Drive or export as MP4/WebM/GIF
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Requires a Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Brave, Edge); Desktop recording outside the browser relies on OS screen sharing permission
  * **Shottr** [https://shottr.cc/]
    - Platforms: macos
    - License: Free personal use, $12 Pro
    - Summary: A tiny, 1.6MB pixel-perfect screenshot utility for macOS with scrolling capture, OCR text extraction, pixel ruler, and blur tools.
    - Advantages: Blazingly fast startup taking less than 15ms to trigger; Scrolling screenshot capture for long web pages and chat logs; Instant OCR extracts text or QR codes directly from screenshots
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: macOS only; Occasional banner prompt to upgrade to the $12 Pro supporter tier
  * **Kap** [https://getkap.co/]
    - Platforms: macos
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/wulkano/kap)
    - Summary: An open-source macOS screen recorder built on web standards that exports silky-smooth video to MP4, GIF, and WebM with custom plugins.
    - Advantages: Clean, unobtrusive menu bar interface with simple capture crop; Export directly to GIF or MP4 with adjustable framerates and dimensions; Extensible plugin system for uploading to S3, Streamable, or Imgur
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: macOS only; Built with Electron, so slightly higher memory footprint during active recording

## 30. Airtable
- Vendor: Airtable
- Category: Business & Analytics
- Typical Commercial Price: Per-seat subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/airtable/
- Verified Free Alternatives (5 tools):
  * **NocoDB** [https://nocodb.com/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: AGPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/nocodb/nocodb)
    - Summary: Turn any database into a smart spreadsheet with grids, forms, kanban, and galleries.
    - Advantages: Airtable-style interface on your own DB; Forms, kanban, and gallery views; Self-hostable
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Fewer automations than Airtable; Self-hosting required for free use
  * **Baserow** [https://baserow.io/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: MIT
    - Summary: An open-source no-code database with spreadsheet-style views, forms, and API.
    - Advantages: Airtable-like UI; Self-host for free; Automatic REST API
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Some premium features are paid; Smaller template library
  * **Grist** [https://www.getgrist.com/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: Apache-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/gristlabs/grist-core)
    - Summary: A modern relational spreadsheet combining the drag-and-drop flexibility of Airtable with real Python formulas and granular permissions.
    - Advantages: Formulas use real Python syntax instead of clunky formula languages; Custom multi-panel dashboards linking tables, cards, and charts; Self-hostable via Docker or use the free cloud tier
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Younger template gallery than Airtable; Python formulas require basic scripting familiarity for advanced features
  * **Teable** [https://teable.io/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: AGPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/teableio/teable)
    - Summary: A super-fast, real-time open-source no-code database built directly on native PostgreSQL, capable of handling millions of records smoothly.
    - Advantages: Blazingly fast performance scaling to 100k+ rows without lag; Native Postgres architecture allows direct SQL queries and extensions; Modern, responsive Airtable-like spreadsheet interface
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Newer product under rapid development; Self-hosting requires Docker compose stack
  * **Mathesar** [https://mathesar.org/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/centerofci/mathesar)
    - Summary: An open-source web application that turns any existing PostgreSQL database into an intuitive spreadsheet UI for non-technical users.
    - Advantages: Zero schema duplication: operates directly on your actual PostgreSQL database; Preserves data types, foreign keys, and constraints automatically; Completely free and open-source with no row limits
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Requires an existing PostgreSQL database; Designed for database administration, not marketing Kanban boards

  * **Proton Drive** [https://proton.me/drive]

    - Summary: Private, end-to-end encrypted cloud storage from the makers of Proton Mail.

    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Smaller free storage than some rivals; Fewer collaboration features

- Category: Security & Privacy
- Typical Commercial Price: Subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/1password/
- Verified Free Alternatives (5 tools):
  * **Bitwarden** [https://bitwarden.com/]
    - Platforms: web, windows, macos, linux, ios, android
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/bitwarden/clients)
    - Summary: An open-source password manager with a generous free plan and apps everywhere.
    - Advantages: Free unlimited passwords on all devices; Open-source and audited; Self-hostable server
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Interface is functional rather than fancy; Some features are premium
  * **KeePassXC** [https://keepassxc.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/keepassxreboot/keepassxc)
    - Summary: A local, offline password manager that stores everything in an encrypted file you control.
    - Advantages: Fully offline and private; Browser integration and TOTP; No account or cloud
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: You handle syncing yourself; No official mobile app
  * **Proton Pass** [https://proton.me/pass]
    - Platforms: web, ios, android, windows, macos, linux
    - License: Free tier, paid plans
    - Summary: An open-source, end-to-end encrypted password manager with hide-my-email aliases.
    - Advantages: Unlimited passwords on the free plan; Built-in email aliases and 2FA codes; Open-source and audited
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Some features need a paid plan; Younger than Bitwarden and 1Password
  * **Passbolt** [https://www.passbolt.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: AGPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/passbolt/passbolt_api)
    - Summary: An open-source password manager designed for agile teams and businesses with granular sharing permissions and OpenPGP cryptography.
    - Advantages: Granular folder and credential sharing permissions for teams; Full OpenPGP end-to-end encryption verified by third-party audits; Free Community Edition can be self-hosted in your own infrastructure
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Designed specifically for team sharing rather than solo consumers; Self-hosting requires standard Docker or Linux server installation
  * **Vaultwarden** [https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: AGPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden)
    - Summary: A lightweight, self-hosted Bitwarden-compatible backend server written in Rust that runs on minimal RAM and unlocks Bitwarden Premium features.
    - Advantages: Drop-in replacement for Bitwarden server using tiny CPU and RAM resources (ideal for Raspberry Pi); Compatible with all official Bitwarden browser extensions and mobile apps; Unlocks premium 2FA features (TOTP generation) and file attachments for free
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Requires basic Docker knowledge to host and maintain; You are responsible for backing up your SQLite/Postgres database

    - Summary: An open-source Firebase alternative built on Postgres with auth, storage, and realtime.
    - Advantages: Real Postgres database; Auth, storage, and realtime included; Can be self-hosted
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Self-hosting has many moving parts; Different data model than Firestore
  * **Appwrite** [https://appwrite.io/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: BSD-3-Clause (Repo: https://github.com/appwrite/appwrite)
    - Summary: An open-source backend server with auth, databases, storage, and functions.

    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Ecosystem is younger than Firebase; Realtime features are less mature

    - Platforms: self-hosted
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase)
    - Summary: An open-source backend in a single file with database, auth, file storage, and an admin UI.
    - Advantages: Single executable, trivial to deploy; Realtime subscriptions and auth; Admin dashboard included
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: SQLite-based, so it is not for huge scale; Pre-1.0 so APIs can change

## 54. Google Chrome
- Vendor: Google
- Category: System Utilities
- Typical Commercial Price: Subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/google-chrome/
- Verified Free Alternatives (4 tools):
  * **Mozilla Firefox** [https://www.mozilla.org/firefox/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: MPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/mozilla/gecko-dev)
    - Summary: The premier independent, open-source web browser that protects your privacy and supports powerful extensions.
    - Advantages: Independent rendering engine (Gecko) not controlled by Google; Full Manifest V2 ad-blocker support; Cross-device sync with privacy protection
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Slightly different performance profile on some sites; Market share is smaller than Chromium
  * **Brave Browser** [https://brave.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: MPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/brave/brave-browser)
    - Summary: A fast, Chromium-based browser with built-in ad, tracker, and fingerprinting blocking by default.
    - Advantages: Blocks ads and trackers out of the box with zero configuration; Runs all Chrome Web Store extensions; 3x faster page loads due to ad stripping
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Includes crypto/rewards features (can be toggled off); Chromium engine
  * **LibreWolf** [https://librewolf.net/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: MPL-2.0 (Repo: https://gitlab.com/librewolf-community/browser)
    - Summary: A custom, hardened build of Firefox focused on privacy, security, and freedom, with zero telemetry.
    - Advantages: Completely removed telemetry and data collection; Pre-configured with uBlock Origin and enhanced tracking protection; DuckDuckGo / SearXNG by default
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Can break logins on high-security banking sites due to strict anti-fingerprinting; No automatic updater on Windows without package managers
  * **Tor Browser** [https://www.torproject.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: BSD-3-Clause
    - Summary: The ultimate privacy browser that bounces your traffic through an encrypted relay network worldwide.
    - Advantages: Complete anonymity and censorship circumvention; Defeats browser fingerprinting completely; Free and non-profit maintained
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Slower browsing speed due to multi-hop routing; Some websites block known exit nodes

    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, android
    - License: Freeware
    - Summary: A modern, multi-threaded download accelerator and torrent client that speeds up downloads by splitting files.
    - Advantages: Up to 10x download acceleration via split connections; Built-in BitTorrent client; Browser integration for Chrome, Firefox, Edge
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Closed source (though completely free); Slightly larger installer than IDM
  * **JDownloader 2** [https://jdownloader.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL
    - Summary: The most comprehensive open-source download manager for hoster sites, link grabbing, and batch extraction.
    - Advantages: Link grabber catches video/audio from thousands of sites; Automatic archive extraction (RAR/ZIP); Captcha solving and cloud remote control
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Java-based interface looks technical; Installer has optional sponsor offers (use clean installer)
  * **Motrix** [https://motrix.app/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/agalwood/motrix)
    - Summary: A gorgeous, minimalist download manager powered by aria2 supporting HTTP, FTP, BitTorrent, and Magnet links.
    - Advantages: Stunning minimalist dark UI; Up to 64 concurrent download threads; No ads or tracking
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Fewer site-specific decrypters than JDownloader; Development is quiet

    - Summary: A collaborative, web-based desktop publishing and brand templating tool with drag-and-drop page layouts and print-ready export.
    - Advantages: Intuitive drag-and-drop page layout inside any modern browser; Real-time collaborative editing with team members; Pre-made templates for flyers, newsletters, and brochures
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Free tier limits stored documents and exports to 3 pages; Cloud-only; requires an internet connection
  * **Typst** [https://typst.app/]
    - Platforms: web, windows, macos, linux
    - License: Apache-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/typst/typst)
    - Summary: A modern, blazingly fast markup-based typesetting system designed to replace LaTeX and InDesign for beautiful reports, books, and papers.
    - Advantages: Instant sub-second compile previews as you type; Clean, intuitive syntax far easier to learn than LaTeX; Produces publication-grade typography, equations, and PDFs
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Markup-driven rather than drag-and-drop GUI; Newer package ecosystem
  * **LyX** [https://www.lyx.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0
    - Summary: A visual WYSIWYM document processor that combines the ease of a graphical word processor with the typographic brilliance of TeX.
    - Advantages: Mathematical formulas and structural formatting look gorgeous; Focus on document structure rather than manual page tinkering; Battle-tested for textbooks, theses, and articles
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Dated graphical interface appearance; Steeper learning curve than standard word processors

## 59. Unity Engine
- Vendor: Unity Technologies
- Category: Developer Tools
- Typical Commercial Price: Subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/unity/
- Verified Free Alternatives (6 tools):
  * **Godot Engine** [https://godotengine.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/godotengine/godot)
    - Summary: The free, open-source 2D and 3D game engine that is completely free of royalties, runtime fees, and subscriptions.
    - Advantages: Open source under MIT license with no runtime fees or royalties; Lightweight 50MB single executable with fast startup; Clean node-based scene architecture with GDScript & C#
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: High-end 3D graphics pipeline still maturing compared to Unreal/Unity; Fewer console export kits out of the box
  * **Defold** [https://defold.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: Defold License (Developer-Friendly) (Repo: https://github.com/defold/defold)
    - Summary: An ultra-lightweight, high-performance 2D and 3D game engine with blazing fast compile times, zero setup, and no runtime royalties.
    - Advantages: Extremely tiny build sizes (under 5MB HTML5/mobile games); Zero royalties or revenue shares ever; Rock-solid Lua scripting workflow
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Smaller 3D feature set compared to Unreal or Unity; Community ecosystem is smaller than Unity
  * **Unreal Engine** [https://www.unrealengine.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: Free to start (5% royalty after $1M gross)
    - Summary: The industry standard AAA 3D game and virtual production engine featuring photorealistic Nanite geometry and Lumen dynamic lighting.
    - Advantages: Unrivaled photorealistic 3D graphics and lighting out of the box; Visual Blueprint scripting plus native C++; 100% free until your game earns over $1,000,000 USD
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Massive disk install size (50GB - 100GB+); Demanding hardware requirements for development
  * **Stride 3D** [https://stride3d.net/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/stride3d/stride)
    - Summary: A free, open-source C# 2D and 3D game engine built on modern .NET, designed as the closest open architectural alternative to Unity.
    - Advantages: Native modern C# and .NET with full async/await support; Familiar component and scene editor workflow for Unity developers; Completely open source with zero runtime fees
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Smaller asset store and plugin ecosystem; Smaller community than Godot or Unity
  * **Raylib** [https://www.raylib.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: zlib/libpng (Repo: https://github.com/raysan5/raylib)
    - Summary: A simple, lightweight C library for videogame programming with no bloated GUI or project managers, beloved by hobbyists and educators.
    - Advantages: Zero bloated editor; pure code-driven videogame programming; Bindings for over 60+ programming languages; Superb cross-platform performance on web, mobile, and desktop
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: No visual drag-and-drop editor; Requires writing game loops and UI manually
  * **GDevelop** [https://gdevelop.io/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: MIT / BSL (Repo: https://github.com/4ian/GDevelop)
    - Summary: An intuitive, open-source 2D and 3D game creator that lets anyone build games using visual event-based logic without writing code.
    - Advantages: Visual event sheet system requires zero coding knowledge; Built-in asset store with thousands of free sprites and sounds; One-click export to iOS, Android, Steam, and web
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Complex game logic can become unwieldy in event sheets; 3D tools are geared toward simple low-poly games

## 61. Adobe Media Encoder
- Vendor: Adobe
- Category: Video & Animation
- Typical Commercial Price: Subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/adobe-media-encoder/
- Verified Free Alternatives (4 tools):
  * **HandBrake** [https://handbrake.fr/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/HandBrake/HandBrake)
    - Summary: The open-source video transcoder for converting video from nearly any format to a selection of modern codecs.
    - Advantages: Massive preset library for devices, web, and streaming; Hardware encoding (NVENC, Intel QSV, Apple Silicon); Batch queue encoding
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Encoding only; does not edit or trim timelines; Cannot decrypt commercial copy-protected Blu-rays natively
  * **Shutter Encoder** [https://www.shutterencoder.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: Free / Donationware
    - Summary: A pro-grade video converter based on FFmpeg tailored for film editors and broadcast workflows.
    - Advantages: Converts to Apple ProRes, DNxHD, H.264, and AV1; Built-in subtitling, rewinding, and audio normalization; No installation needed for portable build
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Interface is dense with professional video specs; Can be intimidating for casual users
  * **Avidemux** [https://avidemux.sourceforge.net/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0
    - Summary: A free, open-source video editor designed for simple cutting, filtering, and re-encoding tasks without quality degradation.
    - Advantages: Cut and splice video segments without re-encoding the stream in "Copy" mode; Batch processing queue for converting libraries of files; Extensive video and audio filter collection (crop, subtitles, deinterlace)
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Basic timeline interface, not designed for multi-track Hollywood editing; No timeline transitions
  * **LosslessCut** [https://github.com/mifi/lossless-cut]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/mifi/lossless-cut)
    - Summary: The Swiss Army knife of lossless video, audio, and subtitle trimming that cuts files instantly at keyframes without re-encoding.
    - Advantages: Blazingly fast cuts in seconds with ZERO loss in video/audio quality; Extract audio tracks, subtitles, or create thumbnail chapters instantly; Supports virtually all video formats powered by FFmpeg
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Cuts only on video keyframes for pure lossless export; Not an effects editor or compositor

    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Steep learning curve; You assemble your own IDE experience
  * **Visual Studio Code** [https://code.visualstudio.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, web
    - License: MIT (source Code-OSS), Microsoft License (official binary) (Repo: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode)
    - Summary: The most popular free code editor with an unmatched ecosystem of extensions, integrated terminal, and debugging tools.

  * **Zed** [https://zed.dev/]
    - Platforms: macos, linux, windows
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/zed-industries/zed)

    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/notepad-plus-plus/notepad-plus-plus)
    - Summary: The legendary lightweight, lightning-fast source code and text editor for Windows that opens gigabyte log files in milliseconds.
    - Advantages: Starts up in a split second with negligible CPU and memory usage; Handles massive multi-gigabyte log files without breaking a sweat; Extensive regex search-and-replace across multiple files and folders
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Native to Windows only (requires Wine on Linux/Mac); Traditional Windows desktop aesthetic
  * **Pulsar** [https://pulsar-edit.dev/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/pulsar-edit/pulsar)
    - Summary: A community-led, fully hackable open-source code editor continuing the beloved legacy and package ecosystem of GitHub’s Atom.
    - Advantages: 100% hackable: customize every piece of the editor via CSS and JavaScript; Familiar Atom package manager and themes; Completely community-driven with zero corporate control
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Electron architecture uses more memory than native C++ editors; Startup speed is slower than Sublime Text

    - License: AGPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon)
    - Summary: The premier decentralized, open-source microblogging network with no algorithms, no corporate ads, and no pay-to-win verification.
    - Advantages: Federated across thousands of independent servers (the Fediverse); Chronological timeline with no manipulative engagement algorithms; No subscription fees, promoted tweets, or data harvesting
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Choosing a starting server can cause initial decision fatigue; Search is deliberately privacy-scoped to hashtags and mentions
  * **Bluesky** [https://bsky.app/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: MIT / Apache-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/bluesky-social/social-app)
    - Summary: An open social network built on the AT Protocol featuring customizable algorithmic feeds, domain-as-handle identity, and composable moderation.
    - Advantages: Fast, responsive interface that feels just like classic Twitter; Algorithmic choice: subscribe to custom feeds created by the community; Use your personal website domain as your verified handle for free
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Direct messaging features are still evolving; Federation with self-hosted instances is in early phases
  * **Nostr** [https://nostr.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nostr)
    - Summary: A lightweight, decentralized protocol for censorship-resistant global publishing where you own your identity via cryptographic keys.
    - Advantages: Decentralized protocol resistant to single-platform account bans or centralized server takedowns; Use any mobile or web client (Damus, Amethyst, Primal, Coracle); Built-in micropayments via Bitcoin Lightning Network zaps
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Requires keeping your private cryptographic key secure; Relay connection concepts differ from standard social logins

    - License: ODbL (Repo: https://github.com/openstreetmap/openstreetmap-website)

  * **Organic Maps** [https://organicmaps.app/]

    - Advantages: 100% offline navigation: download entire countries for trips without cellular data; Zero tracking, zero ads, zero telemetry, and battery-friendly; Detailed hiking trails, cycling routes, and contour elevation maps

  * **OsmAnd** [https://osmand.net/]

    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Deep settings menu can feel overwhelming for basic city driving; Free tier limits number of offline regional map downloads (unlimited on F-Droid)

    - Summary: The world’s leading open-source online survey tool for professional research, universities, and enterprise statistical analysis.
    - Advantages: Unrivaled question type variety and complex multi-page branching logic; Full quota management, token participant tracking, and SPSS export; Completely open-source and self-hostable with unlimited responses
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Traditional survey questionnaire aesthetic rather than sleek one-question cards; Steeper administration learning curve

---

## 70. Squarespace / Webflow
- Vendor: Squarespace / Webflow Inc.
- Category: Business & Analytics
- Typical Commercial Price: Subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/squarespace/
- Verified Free Alternatives (4 tools):
  * **WordPress.org** [https://wordpress.org/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: GPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/WordPress/WordPress)
    - Summary: The open-source content management system that powers over 43% of the web, with tens of thousands of free themes and plugins.
    - Advantages: Zero platform vendor lock-in; host anywhere on affordable servers; Over 60,000 free plugins for e-commerce, SEO, and contact forms; Gutenberg block editor allows visual page building without code
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Requires maintaining your own web hosting and software updates; Too many plugins can slow down site performance if unoptimized
  * **Ghost** [https://ghost.org/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost)
    - Summary: A modern, blazingly fast open-source publishing platform for independent creators, newsletters, and membership websites.
    - Advantages: Built-in native email newsletter delivery and member subscriptions; Ultra-fast Node.js architecture with stellar Core Web Vitals SEO; Clean, distraction-free Markdown and card editor
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Self-hosting requires Node.js and MySQL server administration; Focused specifically on publishing and blogs rather than generic corporate brochure sites
  * **Hugo** [https://gohugo.io/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: Apache-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo)
    - Summary: The world’s fastest open-source static site generator, compiling thousands of pages into static HTML in fractions of a second.
    - Advantages: Generates entire websites in milliseconds with zero database overhead; Host for free on GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, or Netlify free tiers; Static file architecture eliminates dynamic CMS database exploits
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Requires writing Markdown and editing HTML/Go templates; No graphical drag-and-drop web admin interface out of the box
  * **Publii** [https://getpublii.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/GetPublii/Publii)
    - Summary: A privacy-first open-source desktop CMS for creating ultra-fast, secure static websites without touching a code editor.
    - Advantages: Visual desktop app for Mac, Windows, and Linux to write posts and pages; One-click sync to GitHub Pages, GitLab, S3, or standard FTP; Blazingly fast static output with zero server maintenance
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Desktop-based app: editing from a phone or tablet is not supported; Smaller theme marketplace than WordPress

## 71. GoodNotes / Notability
- Vendor: Time Base Technology / Ginger Labs
- Category: Notes & Productivity
- Typical Commercial Price: Subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/goodnotes/
- Verified Free Alternatives (3 tools):
  * **Xournal++** [https://xournalpp.github.io/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/xournalpp/xournalpp)
    - Summary: An open-source handwriting note-taking application with PDF annotation, pressure-sensitive stylus support, and audio recording.
    - Advantages: Annotate and highlight imported PDF textbooks and documents smoothly; Pressure-sensitive pen and stylus support with palm rejection; Audio recording synced to your handwritten notes
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Interface is designed as a desktop application with classic toolbars; Mobile Android port is unofficial/in-progress
  * **Rnote** [https://flathub.org/apps/com.github.flxzt.rnote]
    - Platforms: linux, windows, macos
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/flxzt/rnote)
    - Summary: A vector-based sketch and handwritten note-taking app designed for drawing tablets and touchscreens with smooth infinite canvas.
    - Advantages: Infinite canvas with vector rendering keeps handwriting crisp at any zoom; Shape recognition turns rough sketches into perfect circles and rectangles; Exports to SVG, PDF, and Xopp with full vector fidelity
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Best on Linux and GNOME touchscreens (Windows build is newer); No direct cloud sync client built into the app
  * **Saber** [https://saber.adil.hanney.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/saber-notes/saber)
    - Summary: An open-source handwritten notes app designed for tablets and phones with dark mode inverted ink and Nextcloud synchronization.
    - Advantages: Dark mode inverts colors dynamically so handwriting doesn’t blind you at night; Cross-platform sync via Nextcloud or custom WebDAV servers; Password protect sensitive notebooks with local encryption
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Younger project with fewer template options than GoodNotes; Tool selection is focused on writing essentials

## 72. Audible
- Vendor: Amazon
- Category: Media & Streaming
- Typical Commercial Price: Subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/audible/
- Verified Free Alternatives (3 tools):
  * **Libby by OverDrive** [https://www.overdrive.com/apps/libby]
    - Platforms: ios, android, web
    - License: Free (Library Service)
    - Summary: Borrow thousands of audiobooks and eBooks completely free using your local public library card with no monthly subscription fees.
    - Advantages: 100% free legal access to thousands of bestselling audiobooks and eBooks; Clean, delightful mobile player with sleep timer, bookmarks, and variable speed; Download audiobooks for offline road trips and commutes
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Requires an active public library card; Popular new releases may have digital hold queues before they become available
  * **Audiobookshelf** [https://www.audiobookshelf.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: GPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/advplyr/audiobookshelf)
    - Summary: A self-hosted open-source audiobook and podcast server with dedicated mobile apps for streaming and multi-device progress sync.
    - Advantages: Stream your own audiobook collection anywhere with synchronized playback across devices; Fetches audiobook metadata and chapter covers automatically from open databases; Free, polished native iOS and Android apps
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Requires self-hosting the server via Docker or desktop binary; You provide your own audiobook audio files (MP3/M4B)
  * **LibriVox** [https://librivox.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: Public Domain
    - Summary: A non-profit community of volunteers who record and release free public-domain audiobooks from classic literature.
    - Advantages: Completely free access to over 18,000 public domain audiobooks; Classic literature from Shakespeare and Austen to Doyle and Verne; Download files as DRM-free MP3s with zero registration
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Volunteer narrator quality varies across titles; Covers historic public domain books only (no contemporary copyrighted books)

## 73. Wolfram Alpha Pro
- Vendor: Wolfram Research
- Category: Developer Tools
- Typical Commercial Price: Subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/wolfram-alpha/
- Verified Free Alternatives (3 tools):
  * **GeoGebra** [https://www.geogebra.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: Free for non-commercial use
    - Summary: Dynamic mathematics software that brings together geometry, algebra, spreadsheets, graphing, statistics, and calculus in an intuitive app.
    - Advantages: Interactive visual manipulation of geometric shapes and mathematical functions; Comprehensive CAS (Computer Algebra System) solves equations step by step; Massive free library of classroom interactive simulations
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Non-commercial free license; Interface has many modes which can require exploration
  * **Desmos Studio** [https://www.desmos.com/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux, ios, android, web
    - License: Free web application
    - Summary: A free suite of world-class math tools including the legendary Desmos Graphing Calculator and Scientific Calculator.
    - Advantages: Instant, responsive graph plotting as you type mathematical functions; Sliders, tables of data, animations, and regression curve fitting; Available completely free on the web, iOS, and Android with zero ads
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Specialized in graphing and algebra rather than general computational trivia queries; Step-by-step calculus proofs are limited compared to Wolfram Pro
  * **SpeedCrunch** [https://speedcrunch.org/]
    - Platforms: windows, macos, linux
    - License: GPL-2.0 (Repo: https://github.com/speedcrunch/SpeedCrunch)
    - Summary: A high-precision scientific desktop calculator with auto-completion, historical scrollback, and over 80 built-in math functions.
    - Advantages: Up to 50 decimal digits of precision; Instant calculation as you type with autocompletion of variables and constants; Keyboard-centric workflow makes quick calculations effortless
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Desktop only; no mobile apps; Focused on arithmetic and scientific computation, not symbolic CAS solving

## 74. Bitly / Linktree
- Vendor: Bitly / Linktree
- Category: Business & Analytics
- Typical Commercial Price: Subscription
- Comparison URL: https://appsolutelyfree.com/alternatives/bitly/
- Verified Free Alternatives (3 tools):
  * **Dub.co** [https://dub.co/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: AGPL-3.0 (Repo: https://github.com/dubinc/dub)
    - Summary: A modern open-source link management platform with custom domains, QR codes, geolocation targeting, and rich click analytics.
    - Advantages: Custom domains with automated free SSL certificates; Detailed analytics covering geolocation, referrers, and device types; Generous free tier (25 links/month) or unlimited when self-hosted
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Free cloud tier has monthly link creation limits; Self-hosting requires Next.js and Redis infrastructure
  * **Kutt** [https://kutt.it/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/thedevs-network/kutt)
    - Summary: A modern open-source URL shortener with support for custom domains, link statistics, password protection, and a RESTful API.
    - Advantages: Completely open-source and free to self-host with zero link limits; Set expiration dates and password protection on shortened URLs; Simple, clean web dashboard with QR code generation
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Self-hosting requires Node.js and PostgreSQL/Redis setup; Free public server has occasional registration pauses
  * **BioDrop** [https://biodrop.io/]
    - Platforms: web, self-hosted
    - License: MIT (Repo: https://github.com/EddieHubCommunity/BioDrop)
    - Summary: An open-source link-in-bio platform for developers and creators to connect their community to their content with no paywalls.
    - Advantages: 100% free and open-source with no premium theme paywalls; Add social media icons, blog post links, events, and milestones; Community-driven project backed by open-source contributors
    - Limitations / Trade-offs: Profile updates are configured via JSON or web forms; Fewer commercial e-commerce checkout widgets than Linktree
